feature.title: Gift message on an order
feature.description: Shoppers buying a present want to add a short message that is printed on the packing slip, so the recipient reads it when the parcel is opened. The slip must not show prices, because the recipient should not see what the present cost. Today there is no place to write a message, and shoppers write to support instead, who pass it on by hand and sometimes forget.

context: Worca is how this team ships changes to the online shop. The shop sells household goods to private customers in several countries. Orders are placed by shoppers at checkout, paid, then picked and packed in one warehouse. A packing slip is printed for every parcel and goes inside it. Customer service answers shoppers by email and phone and can see every order. The team prefers small changes that can go live on their own, and wants anything a shopper sees to be tested with real order examples before release.
orientation: The shop already has orders, and each order moves through the statuses placed, paid, packed and shipped. At checkout the shopper fills in an address, picks a delivery option and pays; there is a free-text field called order note, but it is meant for delivery hints such as "leave at the door" and is shown to the courier, not printed on the slip. The packing slip lists the items, the quantities and the prices, and the delivery address. Prices are always shown on it today, and there is no way to switch them off for a single order. Customer service can open an order and add an internal comment, which only staff see. Orders can be changed by the shopper until they are packed, for example the delivery address. Nothing in the shop yet marks an order as a gift. The warehouse works from a pick list that shows one line per item and the order number, with no extra marks.

questions.question: Who writes the gift message?
questions.why: It decides where the message is entered.

questions.question: Where must the message appear?
options: On the packing slip and in the confirmation email
questions.why: It sets how much has to change.

questions.question: Should the packing slip still show prices for a gift order?
questions.why: The shopper wants the recipient not to see what it cost.

goal.text: Shoppers can add a short gift message to an order, and it is printed on the packing slip.
goal.measure: Fewer gift orders end in a customer-service call about the message.
